facts.fact: Equatorial Guinea is one of six CEMAC states covered by GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard, validated by the UMAC ministerial committee in April 2026 and launched on 29 July 2026 over GIMACPAY, in service since 2021.
Equatorial Guinea is one of the CEMAC states on GIMACPAY, the regional platform that processed 20.3 million transactions worth FCFA 863 billion in 2025, with the BEAC among its 153 participants.
BEAC, the central bank of the CEMAC states, joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), per Afreximbank on 9 July 2026, with CEMAC banks to be connected by end-2026.

AfricaNenda says the regional central bank BEAC, whose rules apply to the six CEMAC states including Equatorial Guinea, regulates payment market structures including technical approvals and authorisations of payment solutions.
AfricaNenda says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY, is its overseer and settlement agent, and the switch serves payment providers in Equatorial Guinea.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, provides interoperable payment services to providers in the six CEMAC states including Equatorial Guinea.

TechAfrica News reports on 9 July 2026 that BEAC, which serves Equatorial Guinea among six CEMAC states, has officially joined PAPSS, with PAPSS working with BEAC through end 2026 to operationalise the membership.
Afreximbank's release of 9 July 2026 says BEAC, which serves Equatorial Guinea among six CEMAC states, has officially joined PAPSS, to be operationalised with CEMAC institutions by end 2026.
PAPSS says BEAC, which serves the six CEMAC states including Equatorial Guinea, officially joined PAPSS on 9 July 2026, with operationalisation planned through end-2026.
